metadata.title: Claude making a film about Muse
metadata.audience: anyone who heard Meta's Muse pitch and wants Bear and Claude's read
metadata.source_doc: Bear's pasted doc (2026-10-03): 'Meta Muse: What It Does, Security Concerns, and Business Model'

skin_warnings: BIDEA: palette=claude but the cold open is 'BrutalistHesitantWriter' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. You've heard what Meta tells you about Muse. Now here's what Bear and Claude think — their read on what it does, what it costs, and where the risks are.

show.event: backspaces 'what Meta tells you' → 'what Bear and Claude think' on the spoken correction

props.text:
What is Muse —
what Meta tells you?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the launch-hype framing and corrects it to the opinion framing: Bear and Claude's read.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Six terms. Agent: a program that works for you on its own. Connector: a plug-in to an outside service. Token: a word-sized chunk of text an AI reads or writes. Allow-list: only named things get access. Prompt injection: hidden instructions steer it. Intent layer: where you say what you want.

terms.meaning: a program that works for you on its own
a plug-in to an outside service
where you say what you want

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: six prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Bear and Claude start with Meta's pitch: 'personal superintelligence,' 'AI That Hustles for You.' Unlike a chatbot, it acts — you set a goal; it plans, works the steps, and checks in before anything consequential.

shot.visual_intent: A static speech bubble labeled 'chatbot'; beside it a goal mark, a plan mark, and step marks that build into a flow.
shot.motion_claim: The building flow IS the difference between chatting and acting.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Meta says: launched in the US September 8th, 2026, on Muse Spark, two and a half million downloads in two weeks. In Nik's experience, the model is noticeably less capable than GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable, or Claude Opus.

shot.visual_intent: A timeline tick lands on September 8, 2026; a counter climbs to 2.5M; a small label marks the capability take as Nik's.
shot.motion_claim: The climbing counter is the adoption story; the label keeps the take attributed.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Underneath, their read of the machinery: every user gets a persistent Linux computer in Meta's cloud — browser, filesystem, terminal. Same architecture as Claude Cowork and OpenAI Codex; they differ in audience and default permissions.

shot.visual_intent: Three blocks — model, sandboxed computer, connectors — drop in and stack into one machine.
shot.motion_claim: The stacking blocks are the architecture.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: For consumers it's errands: travel, restaurants, appointments, shopping, forms, negotiating, subscriptions, tickets — Ticketmaster was a launch partner. Their point: its strength is endurance, not intelligence. It keeps going; it isn't especially clever.

shot.visual_intent: A checklist ticks through task after task while a clock spins — relentless, not clever.
shot.motion_claim: Speed plus repetition is the claim; only motion shows it.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: You reach it on web, iPhone, Android, WhatsApp — glasses announced. Connectors skew commerce: Shopify, OpenTable, Ticketmaster, Instacart, Expedia, Stripe. CNBC reported Amazon blocked Muse over its terms. Custom connectors need no Meta review.

shot.visual_intent: Surface marks on top; connector pills below; links draw between them — one pill, marked 'Amazon', is crossed out.
shot.motion_claim: The drawn web is the connector story; the crossed pill is the block.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: For small business — September 29th — it drafts posts and campaigns, reads QuickBooks, works Klaviyo and Shopify. Meta says nothing publishes, sends, or spends without approval. Developers get the Muse Spark API — not the consumer agent.

shot.visual_intent: A split screen: a storefront with an ad draft on the left, a terminal with code on the right.
shot.motion_claim: The split screen holds both audiences at once.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Three tiers, per the document. Free: zero dollars, a hundred million Muse tokens a week. Power: twenty a month, five hundred million. Maximum: a hundred a month, three billion. Same features — you pay for volume. Card required even for free.

shot.visual_intent: A three-column table builds cell by cell: Free $0 / 100M, Power $20 / 500M, Maximum $100 / 3B.
shot.motion_claim: The table IS the content; building it cell by cell paces the numbers.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: The API is priced separately: a dollar twenty-five per million input tokens, four twenty-five per million output. Or ten cents and twenty — if you let them train on your data. Twelve and a half times cheaper on input, twenty-one on output.

shot.visual_intent: An input/output bar pair; then a much smaller pair beside it, labeled 'with data sharing', each tagged with how many times cheaper it is.
shot.motion_claim: Bar lengths make the price gap visible; the multipliers name it.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Bear and Claude's read: that gap isn't a discount — it's a bid. More than ninety percent off, and in return Meta gets whatever you run through it: your usage, your appointments, your purchases, the tickets you pick.

shot.visual_intent: The $1.25 price is struck through and drops to $0.10 with '92% off'; four cards — usage, appointments, purchases, tickets — slide from 'you' into Meta, which grows.
shot.motion_claim: The price falls as the data cards move the other way: the discount IS the payment.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: The business model — their core claim. Primary revenue: transaction fees. A small merchant-paid cut of every purchase Muse brokers, like an affiliate commission. The generous free tier is a bet those fees pay off. You never see a charge.

shot.visual_intent: A shopper mark → Muse → merchant mark flow; a small coin siphons off to Meta.
shot.motion_claim: The siphoning coin is the business model in one motion.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Secondary streams: subscriptions, API sales — and two quieter ones. The ads angle: Meta says no ads inside Muse, but it funnels businesses toward Meta's ad machine, and your browsing shapes ads elsewhere. Plus training data — on by default.

shot.visual_intent: Four small streams — subs, API, ads angle, training — converge into Meta.
shot.motion_claim: Convergence shows many streams, one destination.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Their read of the goal: own the intent layer — shoppers one side, merchants the other, Meta in the middle. The skepticism: one analysis says only eleven of forty-seven payments are automatable. The fees may not carry it — and ads may come.

shot.visual_intent: A funnel: 'I want…' in at the top, Meta in the middle, money out the bottom; then forty-seven coins appear and eleven light up.
shot.motion_claim: The funnel is the strategy; the eleven lit coins are the skepticism.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Now, a hundred million tokens as real work. Nik says he's eighteen percent through this week's free allowance. What's in his folder: thirteen film packages — two hundred twelve beats, about eight thousand words of narration, roughly an hour of film.

shot.visual_intent: A 100M gauge fills to 18% in terracotta; four hero numbers land under it: 13 film packages, 212 beats, 8,149 words, about 62 minutes.
shot.motion_claim: The gauge fills as the folder's contents land: this is what the used share holds.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: At that pace, the full hundred million is about seventy-two film packages a week — nearly six hours of film. Straight-line math from one week; a different week would look different.

shot.visual_intent: The 100M bar fills with five and a half blocks, each one Nik's 18%; two hero numbers land: about 72 film packages, about 5.7 hours.
shot.motion_claim: Repeating the 18% block until the bar is full IS the extrapolation.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: If Muse tokens count like ordinary ones, those eight thousand words are about eleven thousand tokens — under a tenth of a percent of the eighteen million. Claude's read: the rest is the agent re-reading its own work. Tokens measure effort, not output.

shot.visual_intent: A wide bar for 18M tokens with a hairline terracotta sliver at its left; a callout zooms the sliver into a block labeled 'the script', then the rest of the bar is named.
shot.motion_claim: The invisible sliver, zoomed, is how little of the spend is the visible work.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Price it the way Meta prices its API: a hundred million tokens is a hundred twenty-five to four hundred twenty-five dollars. Share your data, and it's ten to twenty. If the tokens compare — nobody can confirm that.

shot.visual_intent: Two range bars: $125–$425 at the standard rate, $10–$20 if you let them train on your data; a caveat line below.
shot.motion_claim: The tiny second bar is the price of letting them keep your data.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Their read: the free tier is a subsidy. Meta is buying a user base — and your data: what you do, what you book, what you buy. So be careful what goes through it. When it's cheap, ask what the discount buys.

shot.visual_intent: A balance: 'free tokens' on one pan, 'your data' on the other; the data pan sinks; a closing line reads 'cheap? ask what the discount buys'.
shot.motion_claim: The beam tipping toward the data pan is the subsidy argument.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concern one: Full Disk Access — the whole disk, not folder-level. Meta says it only touches files you ask about; Bear and Claude call that a behavioral promise, not a technical boundary. The machine can't tell the difference.

shot.visual_intent: A drive outline; a terracotta wash floods the entire thing, edge to edge.
shot.motion_claim: Total coverage, shown totally — the wash is the claim.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concern two: a deny-list, not an allow-list. Nik can't grant one folder — he'd have to block every other disk by name, and any forgotten one is exposed. Fail-safe defaults, violated. Folder pickers could have worked — but Messages, Notes, and Mail need Full Disk Access.

shot.visual_intent: Left: a list being crossed out item by endless item. Right: one folder with a ring around it.
shot.motion_claim: The endless crossing-out versus the single ring IS fail-open versus fail-closed.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Muse told Nik it would only touch one folder. That's a language model's promise — and language models hallucinate. Nik can't set a one-folder limit; it's the whole disk or nothing. A promise isn't a permission system.

shot.visual_intent: A disk with one folder inside; a thin ring labeled 'only this folder' is the promise; the ring stretches out across the whole disk while the disk border stays the only real setting.

show.event: the promise ring around the folder
ring stretches across the whole disk

shot.motion_claim: The ring stretching past the folder is the promise failing with nothing to stop it.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concern three: known vulnerabilities. Malwarebytes reported a zero-day where a dictation redirect could steal an auth token — needs local code execution first. One researcher exported six point eight gigabytes of runtime data, SSH keys included. Plus early prompt-extraction reports.

shot.visual_intent: Three warning triangles land in a row, each labeled: zero-day, data export, prompt extraction.
shot.motion_claim: Three distinct findings, one visual language.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concern four: policy, not cryptography. Training on by default. The ad-systems separation is a policy claim — no independent audit. Every file you ask about is processed in Meta's cloud, and tokens pasted into chat live in the cloud past expiry.

shot.visual_intent: A paper shield labeled 'policy' tears in half; a steel lock labeled 'crypto' holds firm.
shot.motion_claim: The tearing paper is the argument.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concern five: prompt injection and approval fatigue. Any untrusted text — a webpage, an email, a PR, a code comment — can steer the agent, and the failure is adversarial, not random. Approvals only work if you read them; fatigue turns them into reflex.

shot.visual_intent: A page with hidden terracotta text steers an agent dot off course; then approval cards get rubber-stamped faster and faster.
shot.motion_claim: Steering plus the accelerating stamp are both motions.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concern six: trust by design. The mascot, the persona — Bear and Claude call them trust shortcuts. A cute character reads as safe before it's earned it. And 'superintelligence' branding, they say, overpromises for what's really an errand agent.

shot.visual_intent: A cute mascot face; hearts rise from it — then a price tag drops onto it.
shot.motion_claim: The price tag landing on the cute face is the critique.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concerns seven and eight. Business conflicts: affordability advice from the company selling the ads, self-graded attribution, advice that only ever points at Meta inventory. And platform dependence: lock-in, a shopper-optimized roadmap where developer features can vanish.

shot.visual_intent: Two panels: a scale tipping toward ads; a roadmap that shrinks.
shot.motion_claim: The tipping scale and the shrinking roadmap are the two critiques.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Concern nine: the phone. Contacts, messages, health — the mobile permissions expose the most personal data of all. Nik won't use it there.

shot.visual_intent: A phone mark; permission toggles flip on, one after another — contacts, messages, health.
shot.motion_claim: The flipping toggles are the exposure.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: How did Bear resolve it? First: nothing runs locally. The Mac app is gone — signed out, deleted, revoked, verified. Muse is web-only, through muse.ai, ideally in its own browser profile. Not on the phone.

shot.visual_intent: A Mac app icon drops into a trash can; a browser window stays lit.
shot.motion_claim: Removal in motion; what remains is the answer.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: That's the rule that matters most. Muse never runs on Nik's computer. It runs in the cloud, and it only sees what he puts there — a Google Drive folder, a sandbox repo. The wall is where the files live, not what Muse promises.

shot.visual_intent: A laptop labeled 'Nik's computer' is crossed out behind a wall; on the other side a cloud holds Muse, fed by two tiles — a Google Drive folder and a sandbox repo.

show.event: Drive folder and repo feed the cloud

shot.motion_claim: The crossed-out laptop behind the wall IS the boundary: location, not language.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Second: the film setup. Muse works only in its cloud VM, on public sandbox repos. GitHub is a dedicated bot account, sandbox repos only, no pasted tokens. PRs only, branch protection, Claude Code review, deterministic CI — rendering on a burner MacBook with no Muse.

shot.visual_intent: Five stations — VM, PR, review, merge, burner — and a dot travels the pipeline left to right.
shot.motion_claim: The traveling dot is the workflow.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Third: the general rules. Assume breach. Bound the blast radius. Enforce caps outside the agent — a card limit, not an instruction. Irreversible actions get a human. And protect the short list — email, money, credentials, public voice — with real walls, not policies.

shot.visual_intent: A wall; behind it four marks — email, money, credentials, voice.
shot.motion_claim: The wall with the valuables behind it is 'bound the blast radius'.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Six questions stay open. VM disk and compute limits? GitHub connector OAuth scopes? What does a 'Muse token' map to? Will confidential mode ship — with what guarantees? How long does the free tier stay generous? And do ads come to Muse?

shot.visual_intent: Six question marks land in a three-by-two grid.
shot.motion_claim: Open questions, visually open.

qc.sparse_reason: lecture style: one drawn scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Muse is Meta's consumer agent — it acts on errands, with endurance more than intelligence. It costs nothing to start, but the cheapest tokens are paid for with your data; twenty or a hundred dollars a month buys volume, not features. Meta's bet is transaction fees on every purchase it brokers — plus the intent layer itself. The critique: full disk access, a deny-list, real vulnerabilities, and policy where crypto should be. Bear's answer: nothing runs locally — web and cloud only, files in Drive and sandbox repos, reviewed PRs. Open questions: token limits, scopes, confidential mode — and whether the free ride lasts.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. List every AI app on your computer with disk access. For each one, write down whether it uses an allow-list or a deny-list. Then check two things yourself. Did you find every app? And can you say which list model each one uses?

props.command: Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, Full Disk Access — and list every AI app you see
output: Check: you found every AI app with disk access.
Check: you can say allow-list or deny-list for each.
